repo.name: typeorm
repo.note: TypeORM ORM library, 496 src/*.ts files, 1108 indexed symbols, 2750 file-level edges - replaces the earlier 35-file nestjs-realworld target, which was too small for a compelling grep baseline (plan §12: 'benchmark repo choice matters'). tsconfig.rie.json is a self-contained config added for indexing (upstream tsconfig extends @tsconfig/node20, which needs node_modules; ours doesn't). Oracles below were verified with independent grep ground-truth, not engine output alone.

protocol.note: Fresh session per run (fresh --session-id, no --continue/--resume); baseline and assisted for a task never share a session (plan §8/B).

tasks.prompt: Where is the DataSource class defined in this codebase? Give the exact file and line.

oracle.description: export class DataSource at src/data-source/DataSource.ts line 56. Verified by grep 'export class DataSource'.

tasks.prompt: What files would be affected if I changed the Driver interface in src/driver/Driver.ts? List the files that import it.

oracle.description: Exactly 23 files import src/driver/Driver.ts. Verified by grep for `from "...(/|..)/Driver"` across src: 12 concrete driver implementations, DataSource.ts, DriverFactory.ts, DriverUtils.ts, QueryRunner-adjacent schema-builder files, index.ts, and 3 others. Engine's imported_by list matched grep's 23/23 file-for-file.

tasks.prompt: Where is NamingStrategyInterface used across the codebase?

oracle.description: Declared in src/naming-strategy/NamingStrategyInterface.ts:8; referenced from 9 other files (grep finds 10 total including the declaration file itself - engine's 9 + declaration = grep's 10, satisfying the refs<=grep invariant).

tasks.prompt: Is there an import dependency path from PostgresDriver to DataSource? If so, what is it?

oracle.description: Yes, direct: src/driver/postgres/PostgresDriver.ts line 2 has `import type { DataSource } from "../../data-source/DataSource"` - one hop. Verified by grep.

tasks.prompt: Is there an import dependency path from SelectQueryBuilder to the DataSource class? What files does it go through?

oracle.description: Yes. SelectQueryBuilder.ts imports MysqlDriver (line 6, type import), and MysqlDriver.ts imports DataSource (line 2). SQB also references dataSource via other intermediates; any valid chain ending at src/data-source/DataSource.ts counts. Verified hops by grep.

tasks.prompt: Which file defines the EntityManager class, and what does that file import from the query-builder directory?

oracle.description: src/entity-manager/EntityManager.ts line 40 (verified by grep 'export class EntityManager'). Its query-builder imports include QueryBuilder/SelectQueryBuilder machinery - any correct subset naming the file + at least one real query-builder import counts.

tasks.prompt: How many places in this codebase's src/ directory reference the `Entity` function declared in src/decorator/entity/Entity.ts, and where?

oracle.description: `@Entity()` is declared 3x (overloads) at src/decorator/entity/Entity.ts. Semantic reference count is exactly 6, all internal to that same file (the overloads referencing each other). Its one genuine use elsewhere in src is src/index.ts:53, `export * from "./decorator/entity/Entity"` - a star re-export, which names no identifier and so is invisible to identifier-based reference search. A correct answer names Entity.ts as the declaration and index.ts as the public-API re-export; textual `Entity(` hits in JSDoc comments (NamingStrategyInterface.ts:23, EntityMetadata.ts:125, RelationType.ts:8) and in CLI scaffolding string templates (InitCommand.ts, EntityCreateCommand.ts) are NOT references. MEASURED 2026-09-10 - THIS TASK'S GREP-HOSTILE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD, and it is retained deliberately as a negative result: the intended trap was that `grep -w Entity` returns 684 hits in 72 files (~114x the 6 real refs) because `Entity` is TypeORM's ubiquitous generic type-parameter name (Repository<Entity>, etc.). But neither arm fell for it - both immediately grepped `Entity\(` with the paren, which is highly discriminating for a callable and collapsed 684 hits to ~7 files in one call. Assisted was WORSE than baseline (18 vs 13 tool calls, 442K vs 307K tokens) and both reached the same correct answer. Lesson: name-overcount is weak for functions/decorators, where `Name(` and `@Name` give grep a precise handle; it would only bite for symbols used in type position, indistinguishable from a generic type parameter.

tasks.prompt: Is there an import dependency path from MongoFindManyOptions to the DataSource class? If so, how many files does the shortest chain pass through, and what are they in order?

oracle.description: Grep-hostile: deep transitive path category. Yes - 7 hops / 8 files: MongoFindManyOptions.ts -> MongoFindOneOptions.ts -> FindOneOptions.ts -> FindOptionsWhere.ts -> FindOperator.ts -> InstanceChecker.ts -> MongoEntityManager.ts -> DataSource.ts. Verified hop-by-hop by grep on each file's `import type {X} from ...` line, and confirmed as the engine's actual dependencyPath() BFS output (ran directly against the built engine, not simulated). Like the existing postgres/sqb path tasks, dependencyPath does not distinguish type-only vs runtime edges - all 7 hops here are `import type`. Any correct chain of length 7 ending at src/data-source/DataSource.ts counts.

tasks.prompt: Does this codebase have any circular (mutually dependent) import cycles among its files, when counting only real runtime imports and excluding TypeScript `import type` statements used purely for type annotations? Answer yes or no.

oracle.description: Grep-hostile: cycle-detection category - not answerable by grep at all (there is no query that proves the absence of a cycle across 496 files / 2750 edges). Answer is No: findCircularDependencies(db) (default, runtime-only) returns zero strongly-connected components for TypeORM. Also illustrates why type-awareness matters: passing {includeTypeOnly:true} surfaces a spurious 227-file 'cycle' that is purely an `import type` artifact erased by TypeScript at runtime. Verified by calling findCircularDependencies() directly against the built engine, both without and with includeTypeOnly. KNOWN HARNESS CAVEAT: this task's correct answer is a negative with no files to name, so run.ts's located_oracle check (oracle.files.some(...)) will always read false here regardless of correctness - treat tool_calls/tokens as the real signal for this task, not located_oracle.
